purpose: Clone the complete current source body into a separate editable candidate workspace, compare and exercise it, and let the candidate voluntarily request selected merge-readiness observations without changing or automatically approving the live body.

properties.path: candidate body directory; repo-local paths must be under creations/
properties.replace: clone only; optional explicit replacement of an existing candidate directory
properties.timeout_seconds: test/check operations; bounded timeout from 1 through 3600 seconds
properties.readiness_statement: request-merge-check only; the candidate's reason for choosing to request review now
properties.requested_by: request-merge-check only; inspectable identity or role making the request
properties.requested_checks: request-merge-check only; any of source-diff, build, machine-inspect, executable-anatomy, plan-probes, or creation-trials
properties.probe_requests: candidate-local JSON request paths used by selected planning probes or real creation trials

contains: exact_copy_verified or comparison or build result

relationships: clones the current inspectable source body without Git history or runtime output surfaces
keeps candidate edits outside the active machine body
runs the candidate body's own tools/build.py and returns its complete captured build output
lets the candidate choose when to request source, build, anatomy, planning, or creation-trial observations
leaves merge or adoption as a separate explicit choice

anatomy_refs.basis: The capability materializes a separately editable source workspace, verifies the copied bytes, compares candidate and live bodies, and exposes an independent build operation.
The candidate body is assembled from every included current source-body file while explicitly excluding Git history, runtime creations, caches, and short-lived build debris.
The test operation invokes the cloned body's fixed inspectable tools/build.py entrypoint and returns exit state, timeout state, standard output, and standard error.

limitations: this is a source-body clone, not an OS security sandbox; candidate tests run with the current process user's host permissions
Git history, runtime creations, snapshots, caches, and build debris are excluded from the cloned source body
included symbolic links are rejected because link-preserving clone semantics are not implemented
the current operation can clone, inspect, test, and request a merge check; it does not automatically merge, approve, or adopt a candidate body
readiness is candidate-declared and is not produced by a score, cadence, or workspace-manager decision
a passing build proves only the checks implemented by that candidate body's build
persistent_state: the caller-selected candidate workspace remains editable until deliberately removed or adopted

truth.basis: The exact copy result, exclusions, source comparison, captured build output, execution boundary, and lack of automatic adoption are explicit.

agency.basis: The candidate is free to diverge in its separate body, while humans or AIs retain the explicit choice of what to edit, test, keep, or later adopt.

continuity.basis: Experiments accumulate in an editable candidate body without rewriting the continuing live body.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: The machine can run its real build on a complete candidate body and inspect the resulting differences before any separately chosen adoption.
